claim: Junyo and Ryujo (Kakuta's Second Mobile Striking Force) were committed to the Aleutians operation (Operation AL) in June 1942 and not to the Midway carrier force; the Naval General Staff insisted on the Aleutians operation as the price of approving the Midway plan
source: Naval History and Heritage Command, H-Gram 016-2 'The Aleutians Campaign, 1942-43'; Wikipedia, Battle of Dutch Harbor
note: The NHHC says Operation AL was not a diversion. The report says the Army set the price for its support; the NHHC says the Navy General Staff did. That wording is to be checked.

claim: Yamamoto's Main Body, with the battleships, sailed about 300 miles behind Nagumo's carriers; the distance is criticized for leaving the carriers without the battleships' scouts and anti-aircraft guns
source: Wikipedia, Battle of Midway; USMC history, Japanese plans for Midway; SOFREP summary of Parshall and Tully
note: The number of battleships in the Main Body differs between sources; the report states none.

claim: Some of Nagumo's staff argued for a further strike on the oil tanks and dockyards after the two waves, and Nagumo, advised by Kusaka, retired as planned for fear of the missing American carriers
source: Toland's account via weaponsandwarfare.com and lnlpublishing.com
note: Fuchida's account of the bridge argument is disputed; Genda is said to have denied it. The report says 'some of Nagumo's own staff argued' and nothing about who. The claim that the oil tanks held millions of barrels was NOT used because no source was found.

claim: Churchill diverted the 7th Division convoy toward Rangoon in February 1942 and Curtin refused; two brigades of the 6th Division (16th and 17th) garrisoned Ceylon from March to August 1942
source: Australian War Memorial and DFAT, Documents on Australian Foreign Policy vol. 5 (cables of 20 and 23 February 1942); anzacportal.dva.gov.au
note: The Ceylon garrison followed the Burma dispute and was not part of it; the third order is a modeled compromise and says so.

claim: The 32nd Division, a National Guard division with little jungle training, was sent to Papua from mid-September 1942, one regiment airlifted and others by sea and on foot; it entered combat at Buna on 16 November
note: The report does not claim the division was sent to Kokoda; the third order is a modeled alternative.

claim: Stalin told Harriman in June 1944 that American bombers could use six or seven of twelve suitable airfields between Vladivostok and Sovetskaya Gavan; at Yalta in February 1945 he did not object to American bases at Komsomolsk and Nikolaevsk
source: FRUS 1944 vol. IV; FRUS Malta and Yalta
note: That no base was built is from memory and unchecked.

claim: The aerial mining of Japanese waters (Operation Starvation) began in late March 1945 under XXI Bomber Command; 12,135 mines laid, 670 ships sunk or damaged
A diversionary carrier raid on Jaluit by Task Force 11 (Lexington) was part of the December 1941 plan for relieving Wake
source: War History Online, 'The relief of Wake Island 1941'; World War II Database
note: The sources do not say the raid was cancelled, and the report no longer claims it.

claim: Horii's detachment reached Ioribaiwa ridge, about thirty miles from Port Moresby, in September 1942
source: Wikipedia, Battle of Ioribaiwa and Tomitaro Horii (about 50 km, roughly 30 miles, from Port Moresby; withdrawal ordered from Imperial Headquarters)

claim: The Army's 2nd Division was delivered to Guadalcanal by destroyer transports in October 1942; the 38th Division and Tanaka's role in the destroyer runs are not confirmed today
source: Wikipedia, Tokyo Express and Naval Battle of Guadalcanal (the 2nd Division, eight night runs)
note: To be checked: the 38th Division and Tanaka.

claim: Nishimura's Southern Force went through Surigao Strait separately from Kurita's Center Force through San Bernardino Strait; the battleship Fuso and Yamashiro were with Nishimura
source: Britannica and the NHHC overview of Leyte Gulf (see battles-round2.json)
note: That Ugaki was Kurita's battleship division commander (the adviser) is from memory.
